title: Splunk Core Certified Power User
summary: The Splunk Core Certified Power User credential, exam code SPLK-1002, is the second step in the Splunk certification path and sits above the entry level Core Certified User. It is aimed at analysts, engineers and security operations staff who already run basic searches and now need to build their own knowledge objects. The exam is multiple choice and asks you to write and read Splunk search language, so it tests command knowledge and settings rather than administration of the platform. A pass shows an employer that you can turn raw machine data into reusable searches, tags, event types, macros, data models and workflow actions. The sections below follow the published blueprint, including its percentage weights; check the vendor's current version before booking. The credential supports roles such as security operations analyst, Splunk analyst and observability engineer. This page is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with Splunk.

beginner.definition: SPLK-1002 is a Splunk exam for people who use the search language every day. The full title is Splunk Core Certified Power User, and the exam code is SPLK-1002. It sits above the entry level Core Certified User credential, so you should already be able to run simple searches. The exam checks that you can filter results, correlate events and build reusable knowledge objects.
beginner.whyItMatters: Many security and IT teams run on Splunk, and the people who can shape data quickly are the most useful. This certification proves that you can go beyond copying an existing search. It shows that you can build your own fields, tags, macros and data models. That skill shortens investigation time, because a good search can be reused and a weak one is repeated by hand. It also prepares you for the advanced power user and administrator certifications. Many employers list it for security operations roles.
howItWorks: Practice in a free Splunk instance with sample data, because the exam rewards fast recall of the search language.
Learn the transforming commands first, starting with chart and timechart for simple visualizations.
Move on to eval, search, where and fillnull, then write each command from memory.
Study one knowledge object group at a time, such as field extractions, then tags and event types.
Build a small data model and use the Common Information Model add on so the ideas become concrete.
Check the published blueprint before you book, because Splunk numbers the sections and gives each one a weight.
beginner.example: Imagine that you work in a security operations center that receives firewall logs. A manager asks how many blocked connections came from each country last week. At first you run the search by hand and paste the result into a report. Later you notice that the same question returns every Monday. You create a calculated field and add a tag. You save a macro and place the result in a dashboard that refreshes itself. The manager now reads the answer without asking you. The Power User exam covers each of those steps, from simple transforming commands to reusable knowledge objects.
takeaways: SPLK-1002 is a search language exam, so daily practice beats reading.
The blueprint gives every section a weight, so plan your study time with those numbers.
Finish the Core Certified User material first, because the basics are assumed.
